label: rem:isospin-singlet-binds-more-two-nucleon-reading
title: Which two-nucleon channel the singlet ordering selects
html:
This remark records how the ordering \mu_- < \mu_+ of the isospin interface scalars is read against the measured two-nucleon channels, and the values of the two scalars at q_0.

What it selects

Binding is B = -\alpha\log\mu with \alpha > 0, a decreasing function of \mu, so the smaller scalar is the more strongly bound channel. The singlet is thus predicted to bind harder than the triplet at every q, and nature agrees: of the four two-nucleon channels --- pp, nn and pn({}^1S_0), all T = 1, against pn({}^3S_1), the deuteron at T = 0 --- exactly the T = 0 channel binds.

The selection is made by a representation label. There is no crossing count, no per-species multiplicity m_{pp}, m_{nn}, m_{pn} to choose, and consequently nothing to tune: the channel is picked out by which isospin block of H_2(q) its weight comes from. The alternative story, in which the interface is keyed on the nucleon content of the pair, is not only unnecessary; it is unavailable --- see the content-keyed refutation.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall: it invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs --- real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical or q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here. At q_0 = 1.10997858275138080759 the two scalars are \mu_- = 0.24729788674803459841 and \mu_+ = 0.75270211325196540159.
